status: Fix installed as unchanged 1.0.1 (25). Shared renderer regressions pass; complete physical-device Pearl export decoded and visually reviewed at 22 matched frames.

source.fixture_provenance: Six actual 720x1280 decoded source frames and the original saved appearance masks; fits measured from the current-frame pixels before this fix. Five observed round contact masks and one printed-panel undersizing case.
source.build_number_policy: Keep the current development version and build number until the user decides to upload TestFlight.

causes.problem: Flat or faceted edges during small movements
causes.cause: Any smear over 0.75 source pixels allowed full owned-mask alpha along the motion axis, outside the smooth swept body. Model sampling/crop edges became the replacement outline.
causes.fix: Bound motion-driven mask restoration to the swept body envelope. Independently supported blur lobes can still extend coverage. The mask can keep the swept body opaque without restoring unsupported outer edges.

causes.problem: Undersized replacement on a printed-panel fit
causes.cause: A failed edge fit below the mask-derived radius band was clamped toward the lower bound, shrinking a round ball.
causes.fix: When the mask has a physical covariance axis ratio at most 1.15, use its independent circle for an undersized rejected fit. Elongated/occluded masks retain the previous bounded fit and blur treatment.

scope.replay_and_export: Same shared coverage function, no cached output reuse.
scope.additional_work: Three second-moment sums added to the existing mask loop; maximum coverage accumulated in the existing smear loop. No extra passes or image/model buffers.
scope.live_recording_note: Current live camera presentation uses the matched source image and glow trail. Opaque skin replacement is the replay/export path; no new live skin picker added.

existing_ios_tests.note: The other two tests in this run are the new contour regressions. The printed-panel case passed; the contour case initially used strict less-than 1 pixel and found exactly 1 pixel at one swept edge. The final test explicitly allows at most one pixel, including 0.1px scan quantization.
